editor.san3Title: Romance of the Three Kingdoms III (Mega-CD)
editor.san3Description: For the original Japanese Mega-CD edition. Capture at a strategic command menu to edit campaign data; save in the game to retain it. Historical base abilities are read-only. Creation defaults (before allocation) and battle edits are temporary memory operations; keep checkpoints for them. Reopen game panels after editing.
editor.phantasyStar4Description: Verified with Ken Tse Chinese 1.6 Original mode. Return to a field/menu outside battle and use Capture for editing before each session. Resume and save inside the game to retain changes in its native save. Later level-ups and hardware events can reset attributes, learned abilities and their limits. Stacked-inventory translations and MODs are not supported.
editor.jinyongDescription: For the original DOS game, not MODs or remakes. Synchronize R1/R2/R3.GRP, S1/S2/S3.GRP and D1/D2/D3.GRP together. Only R files are edited. Reload the in-game save after editing; changes do not update game memory.
editor.unsupported: Editing is not supported for this game release or progress type.
editor.saveRequired: Save inside the game and synchronize to your account first, or import a native game save.
editor.noChanges: There are no changes to save.
editor.title: Save editor
editor.saved: Edits were saved as a new revision. Check the game window for synchronization results.
editor.stale: A newer save exists. Your draft is retained. Review it before reloading.
editor.pendingChanges: {count} unsaved edit across all files and slots | {count} unsaved edits across all files and slots
editor.koukaiDescription: For the DOS PC edition's 10-slot KOUKAI2.DAT save format. Add the save path to the synchronization list. Administrators must confirm that the game version is suitable.
editor.batchHelp: Only explicitly changed numeric fields are copied. Names and structural operations are excluded. Every target must be valid; review before saving.
editor.captureRequired: Capture the paused game again before editing. Applying changes or resuming play ends the previous editing session.
